newsitem.title: USA: Suspect package at State Department is calendars.
newsitem.headline: Suspect package at State Department is calendars.

text.p: Bomb squad investigators were called in to examine a suspicious package at the U.S. State Department on Tuesday but it turned out to be a bundle of old NATO calendars, a spokesman said.

The spokesman, Nicholas Burns, said the State Department's diplomatic security agents "quite appropriately" called in the experts after finding the package in a closet next to a fire extinguisher on the second floor of the building.
"They called the (Washington) D.C. bomb squad, which came to look at the package. It turned out to be a package of 1996 NATO calendars," Burns told a regular department briefing.
"I hope this isn't a bad omen for 1997, which is supposed to be the year of NATO," he added.

The scare came the day after three letter bombs were found at the United Nations, all addressed to the U.N. bureau of the Arabic-language newspaper Al-Hayat. A series of letter bombs has been sent this month, apparently from Egypt, to addresses in the United States and Britain.

Burns said the agents "did the right thing, because...when there are suspicious packages, you're conservative in the way you look at them and you take take all appropriate measures, including if necessary caling in the bomb squad."
